comparison: Both evaluations support the finding that existing pain signatures (NPS, SIIPS, etc.) do not predict facial expression (C23-C27). OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor while peer reviewers affirm the distinctiveness of FEPS with 'minimal overlap' with other pain signatures.

Both support the machine learning methodology and FEPS development (C28-C29). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation noting modest R² (0.22), while peer reviewers praise the 'rigorous approach' and 'solid' analyses. Peer review also encompasses broader claims about FEPS characteristics (C30-C37, C54) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

OpenEval evaluates spatial distribution and functional interpretation of FEPS (C30-C34, C54) as supported with appropriate anatomical localization. Peer reviewers address these claims as part of their broader acceptance of the FEPS methodology and findings.

OpenEval supports the statistical comparison showing distributed activity is necessary (C35-C36). Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of their overall affirmation of the FEPS approach and findings.

Perfect claim overlap (C38-C40). Both evaluations support the specificity analyses showing FEPS responds to pain with facial expression. OpenEval notes p=0.07 is marginal, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings without challenge.

Both support the low cosine similarity findings (C45-C46, C55) demonstrating FEPS distinctiveness. OpenEval cautions that 'minimal or no overlap' may be overstated, while peer reviewers affirm the FEPS is 'complementary' with 'minimal overlap' with other pain signatures.

Both support network-level similarities (C47-C49, C51). OpenEval notes functional interpretations are speculative but appropriately cautious. Peer reviewers accept these regional overlaps as consistent with 'minimal' rather than 'no' overlap.

Perfect claim overlap (C93-C96). Both evaluations support the mixed-effects modeling showing FEPS predicts facial expression independent of pain ratings. OpenEval notes the interaction effect is small, while peer reviewers accept the strong FEPS-expression relationship.

Perfect claim overlap (C76-C77). Both evaluations support the lack of association between pain ratings and facial expression. OpenEval emphasizes this validates independence in the constant-stimulus design, while peer reviewers view it as consistent with complementary information.

Perfect claim overlap (C78). Both evaluations support the temporal stability analysis. OpenEval emphasizes this validates that FEPS is not confounded by time effects, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this quality control finding.

Perfect claim overlap (C99-C106). Both evaluations support the authors' acknowledgment of model limitations. OpenEval views the honest assessment as strengthening the evaluation, while peer reviewers accept the transparent discussion of limitations.

High claim overlap (C107-C111). OpenEval supports the authors' acknowledgment of specificity limitations as honest and appropriate. Peer reviewers also address these limitations (R11) but evaluate them as UNCERTAIN, viewing the lack of specificity testing as a critical weakness that undermines conclusions, not just a limitation for future work.

OpenEval supports the acknowledgment that separate AU analysis is needed (C112-C113). Peer reviewers address this as part of broader specificity concerns (R11), emphasizing these limitations as critical weaknesses requiring resolution.

Both address main conclusions about FEPS distinctiveness and pain complexity (C4-C6, C55-C56, C114-C115). OpenEval finds conclusions supported by empirical findings. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, affirming distinctiveness but raising significant concerns about specificity claims, stating authors only 'partially succeed' in their aims.

Both address regional overlaps between signatures (C41-C44, with R5 also covering C47, C49, C51). OpenEval supports these observations as contextualizing distinctiveness claims. Peer reviewers accept these findings as consistent with 'minimal' overlap.

OpenEval supports the functional interpretation of distributed FEPS pattern (C37) while noting causal mechanisms cannot be established. Peer reviewers address this claim as part of their broader acceptance of FEPS methodology and characteristics.
OpenEval evaluates study sample and procedures (C57-C64) as supported with appropriate documentation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these methodological details.

OpenEval evaluates stimulus delivery and rating procedures (C65-C71) as supported with appropriate individualized calibration. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these methodological details.

OpenEval evaluates facial expression measurement methodology (C72-C74) as supported using validated FACS, though notes inter-rater reliability not reported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these measurement details.
OpenEval evaluates fMRI acquisition and preprocessing (C79-C86) as supported with standard, appropriate procedures. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these technical details.

OpenEval evaluates the spatial autocorrelation correction method (C98) as supported and representing best practices. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this statistical methodology.
